headline: Graph and pairwise models infer regulatory and drug-linked networks from omics data
label: Graph Learning For Biological Networks
summary: Topology-aware graph models are being fused with pairwise learning and cellular lineage to prioritize regulatory and drug-association edges.
synthesis: The common thread is graph-structured learning over biological networks, where relational topology is modeled explicitly rather than reduced to flat feature tables. In gene regulatory network inference, scGPL couples global regulatory graph topology with pairwise TF-target interactions on scRNA-seq data, scPhyloGRN adds cellular lineage topology to prioritize TF-target edges, and CausalODE optimizes a causal reach metric over latent mediator dynamics from Perturb-seq. Drug-centred work applies comparable multi-view designs: GLH2Syn combines global diffusion with local structure in a heterogeneous hypergraph for drug synergy, MTDKF fuses metapath topology with domain knowledge for miRNA-drug-disease triplets, and MulDR preserves omics-specific cell-line relations. HV-MultiScaleGNN compares local, global, and combined graph views for host-virus protein interactions. The distinctive element is the separation and recombination of local and global relational views, or of topology and auxiliary knowledge, rather than a single pooled graph.
